gaps.sentence: She's ___ charge of the whole marketing department.
I'll be there ___ ten minutes at the latest.
gaps.explanation: 'in ten minutes' = after ten minutes have passed.

gaps.sentence: He stayed ___ touch with every colleague he'd ever had.
The proposal was rejected ___ a single vote.
gaps.explanation: 'by a single vote / by two goals' — the margin takes 'by'.

gaps.sentence: The old theatre is ___ threat of demolition.
___ good fortune, nobody was hurt in the collapse.
gaps.explanation: 'through good fortune' = by means of luck.

gaps.sentence: The letter arrived ___ due course — three weeks later.
gaps.hint: ___ due course = at the expected time
gaps.explanation: 'in due course' = at the proper time eventually.

gaps.hint: to his credit = in his favour
gaps.explanation: 'to somebody's credit' — something in their favour.
